                      [32m'**Database seeding** is a term for populating the database with some initial data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is where `wasp db seed` comes in!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Now, Wasp allows you to write a JS/TS function, import any server logic (including Actions) into it as you wish, and then seed the database with it.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-02, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.11.8/data-model/backends)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can define as many **seed functions** as you want in an array under the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'app.db.seeds\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- TypeScript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'prismaClient\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m', which is a Prisma Client instance used to interact with the database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is the same Prisma Client instance that Wasp uses internally and thus includes all of the usual features (e.g., password hashing).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since a seed function falls under server-side code, it can import other server-side functions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Run the command\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Alternatively, run the command\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db seed <seed-name>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'to choose a specific seed function right away, for example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wasp db seed devSeedSimple\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Use one of the following commands to run the seed functions:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'prisma migrate dev\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'This command:\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Try https://sqitch.org/ or https://flywaydb.org/ for secure database migrations and store them in your version control system.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Then you can pull the live database unidirectionally into both your staging and development environments, letting the migrations handle the schema updates.\n'[39m +

Wasp automatically invalidates a Query\'s cache whenever an Action that declares the *same* Entity runs. This automatic, entity-based invalidation is convenient but coarse: it does not understand *derived* or *relational* data, so a computed Query that depends on another entity only through a relation will NOT be refreshed automatically. Your job is to build a small task board that relies on automatic invalidation where it works and falls back to explicit React Query cache management where it does not.  A Wasp project skeleton already exists at the project path. Because of that, adding or toggling a task will NOT automatically refresh it. You must keep it up to date on the client yourself using React Query\'s cache mechanisms: obtain the `QueryClient` (react-query is bundled with Wasp and importable from `@tanstack/react-query`) and invalidate/refetch the stats Query after the relevant Actions. A Wasp client Query object exposes its cache key via its `queryCacheKey` property, which you can use as the react-query query key. - Compute the derived statistics from the database (e.g. via the Project entity\'s Prisma relation / relation counts); do not maintain a separate hand-rolled counter table. - Use a local SQLite database (the default dev database). Running it should clear any prior projects/tasks first so the result is deterministic. The seed is run with `wasp db seed devSeed`. - Project path: /home/user/taskboard - Start command (run from the project path): `wasp start`. The first build can take a while before the page becomes available. - The page must render the following stable, machine-checkable markers so the UI can be inspected reliably (attributes are on the element whose text is read):   - For each project, show its name, and an element with attribute `data-testid="stat-total-<projectId>"` whose text content is exactly the project\'s total task count as a number, and an element with attribute `data-testid="stat-done-<projectId>"` whose text content is exactly the project\'s done-task count as a number.   - For each task, an element with attribute `data-testid="task-<taskId>"`, and a clickable button with attribute `data-testid="toggle-<taskId>"` that toggles that task\'s done state.   - For each project, a clickable button with attribute `data-testid="add-task-<projectId>"` that adds a new task to that project (the new task\'s title may be any non-empty string).   - `<projectId>` and `<taskId>` are the numeric database ids of the project and task.                   {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Implement query invalidation via entities · Issue #64 · wasp-lang/wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2020-09-30, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/wasp-lang/wasp/issues/64)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Stemming from #63, we want to implement first version of "entities as resources" solution.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This means following:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Instead of directly importing and using prisma client, from now on Entities are to be declared for each operation and then injected into it, probably via context.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Based on declared entities, actions will invalidate appropriate queries: if action A uses entity E, and action A is performed, then all queries also using entity E should be invalidated.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'entities: [Task, Project]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'where entities is optional and default value is [].\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Then, in query/action, we will access operation like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (args, context) => {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Is there a correct way to pass context data to each query? #20907\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# A dive into Wasp; a domain-specific language for building full stack web ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-01-24, last updated: 2026-07-10, [Read more](https://blog.openreplay.com/a-dive-into-wasp/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp describes database mode as `entities` - this is a thin layer over the Prisma Schema Language (remember Wasp uses Prisma DB).\n'[39m +

            [32m'## Task States and Management\n'[39m +

          description: [32m'Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.\n'[39m +
            [32m'When using the newTask tool, you may specify a agentType parameter to select which agent type to use.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent can analyze code and create review comments on specific lines.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "review the code in src/auth"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "add review comments to this file"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### walkthrough\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to create a summary of the changes made in the current task.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to documentation and explanation; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "summarize what we have done"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a walkthrough for the changes"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "explain the changes made in this task"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the readFile tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report. Therefore, your prompt should contain a highly detailed task description for the agent to perform autonomously and you should specify exactly what information the agent should return back to you in its final and only message to you.\n'[39m +
